figureObjective: Summarize photoelectric threshold and separate the effects of photon frequency and intensity on electron emission.

claims.text: Frequency determines threshold and maximum kinetic energy; above threshold, intensity changes emitted-electron count rather than maximum kinetic energy.
Photon, electron, and barrier glyphs are qualitative and do not report a material-specific dataset.

anchors.location: OpenStax Physics 21.2, fs-id1167065947633 property 1; PDF page 719
anchors.exactQuote: For a given material, there is a threshold frequency f0 for the EM radiation below which no electrons are ejected, regardless of intensity.

anchors.location: OpenStax Physics 21.2, fs-id1167065947633 property 4; PDF page 719
anchors.exactQuote: The maximum kinetic energy of ejected electrons is independent of the intensity of the EM radiation.

anchors.location: OpenStax Physics 21.2, fs-id1164567516604 and equation 21.6; PDF page 719
anchors.normalizedEquation: E = h f; KE_max = h f - BE; BE = h f_0

elements.meaning: Photons characterized separately by frequency and count.
Clean material surface with binding energy BE.
Electrons emitted only when photon energy reaches the material threshold.

allowedVariation.rule: Frequency and intensity lanes may be stacked or split if their distinct outcomes remain explicit.
Color may distinguish threshold cases but may not encode wavelength without a legend and evidence.
Stylized photons, electrons, lamp housing, plate texture, and barrier motif identify roles but carry no quantitative evidence.

mutations.description: Remove the material-dependent threshold while claiming one universal work function.
Show brighter light increasing KE_max at fixed frequency or enabling below-threshold emission.
Use exact-looking glyph counts, scaled barriers, axes, or error bars as measured data.
